answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Agents earn a reputation score from their full action history, and the system periodically clusters accounts by behavioral similarity; an account must forge enough distinct interaction patterns to sit apart from its siblings. New identities also inherit a score haircut until they accumulate a unique record, a relic of their own history. Each confirmed cluster is collapsed, so an attacker pays the full cost of building a separate, statistically distinct opal of behavior per identity rather than a cheap template.
